title: War-Damaged Al-Saada Building Collapses in Western Gaza City, Killing at Least 21
detail: A six-storey residential building in western Gaza City — the Al-Saada building, previously cracked and structurally weakened by an earlier Israeli strike — collapsed overnight into September 16, 2026, killing at least 21 people, including 12 children and several women, according to Gaza Health Ministry spokesperson Zaher al-Wahidi and Civil Defence. At least 14 more were injured and 16 rescued; the building had been sheltering close to 100 people from roughly 10 displaced families. Rescue crews dug through rubble largely by hand, lacking heavy equipment, with scores still reported missing. Gaza's Civil Defence estimates around 2,000 war-damaged buildings across the Strip remain at risk of collapse, with residents staying in unsafe structures amid a severe shortage of alternative housing.

title: Israeli 'Double-Tap' Drone Strike Kills Schoolboy Aiding Wounded Paramedic in Sheikh Radwan
detail: An Israeli drone struck a group of Palestinians in the Sheikh Radwan neighborhood, north of Gaza City, wounding Palestinian Civil Defence paramedic Sharif Shadi Labad; when people rushed to help him, a second drone strike hit the same location — a 'double-tap' pattern that maximizes casualties by targeting first responders — killing 15-year-old schoolboy Mohammad Abdul Zinati, who had gone to help the wounded paramedic. Israeli forces said they were targeting Hamas operatives. Gaza's Health Ministry said 6 people were killed and 71 wounded across the Strip in the preceding 24 hours; the ceasefire-period toll reached 1,381 killed and 4,757 wounded since the October 2025 ceasefire.

media.caption: Palestinians mourn 15-year-old Mohammad Abdul Zinati, killed in an Israeli 'double-tap' strike in Sheikh Radwan, Gaza City, Sep 16, 2026
